summary: Dilbert cartoonist Scott Adams turned a belief in affirmations and his own persuasive powers into online grievance, blaming diversity for his setbacks until racist remarks got his strip dropped in 2023.

evidence.note: Adams is six in 1963, placing his birth around 1957
start of long segment on his turn to affirmations and New Thought ideas
his later claim that bank diversity policy blocked his promotion
Dilbert is syndicated and spreads to 50 then 100 papers by 1990-91
his claims about affirmations working, framed as hacking reality
2008 book blames diversity and Black-led programming for the TV show's cancellation
2011 blog post about women and the sock puppet defence that followed
Trump-era punditry and Win Bigly persuasion claims online
stepson's brain injury, addiction and 2018 fentanyl overdose death
2023 racist remarks lead newspapers and syndicate to drop the strip

notes: Adams was alive when this aired in 2023; lifespan end 2026 reflects his death in January 2026, after release. Covered span runs to the 2023 release. Primary theme is racism since the arc ends in his racist breakdown; self-help and affirmations are the other main thread. Holocaust-numbers questioning and the vaccine claims are short segments and were not tagged.
